title: Motor Claim Damage Assessment from Photos
summary: Detect damaged panels and damage types from guided claim photos, check them against the workshop estimate and pre-inspection images, and give surveyors a structured evidence pack.

seo.title: Motor Claim Damage Assessment from Photos | VipraTech
seo.description: Computer vision that detects vehicle damage from claim photos, checks workshop estimates and pre-inspection images, and prepares evidence for surveyors.

problem.intro: A motor own-damage claim usually starts with photos taken at the roadside or the garage, followed by a workshop estimate listing parts to replace and labour to charge. Surveyors compare the two, often across many claims a day, and decide what was damaged in this accident, what can be repaired and what was already there.

pain_points.title: Surveyor capacity is stretched
pain_points.detail: Surveyors travel between workshops and review photo sets remotely, and simple claims wait behind complex ones.

pain_points.title: Estimates drift from the damage
pain_points.detail: Workshop estimates can include replacement of parts that look repairable or that show no visible damage in the photos.

pain_points.title: Old damage and reused photos
pain_points.detail: Pre-existing dents, photos from a previous claim or images taken before the policy began are hard to catch without side-by-side comparison.

pain_points.title: Poor photo sets cause rework
pain_points.detail: Blurred, dark or incomplete photos mean another visit or another request to the customer, which delays the repair.

solution.overview: We build a computer vision service that receives guided photos from your self-inspection app or a WhatsApp link, checks that they are usable and cover the required angles, and then detects vehicle parts and damage types such as dents, scratches, cracks, broken glass and deformation. Each damaged panel gets a severity estimate and a repair-or-replace suggestion. The service reads the workshop estimate and highlights lines with no matching visible damage, compares photos with pre-inspection or earlier-claim images to spot pre-existing damage, and checks image metadata for reuse. Surveyors receive a damage map and evidence pack and make the assessment.
capabilities: Guided capture checks for blur, lighting, distance and required angles, with instant retake prompts
Detects vehicle parts and damage types per panel, with a severity estimate and confidence
Suggests repair or replace per part, using your surveyor guidelines as the reference
Reads the workshop estimate and flags parts or labour lines with no matching visible damage
Compares with pre-inspection and earlier claim photos to highlight pre-existing damage
Checks image metadata and near-duplicates to catch reused or out-of-period photos

workflow.title: Capture guided photos
workflow.detail: The customer, garage or field inspector follows an on-screen guide in the app or a WhatsApp link.

workflow.title: Check photo quality
workflow.detail: Blur, lighting and angle coverage are checked, and missing or unusable shots are requested again immediately.

workflow.title: Detect parts and damage
workflow.detail: Models identify panels and damage types and estimate severity for each.

workflow.title: Compare with estimate and history
workflow.detail: The workshop estimate, pre-inspection photos and earlier claims are compared with the detected damage.

workflow.title: Flag mismatches
workflow.detail: Estimate lines without visible damage, possible pre-existing damage and reuse signals are flagged.

workflow.title: Surveyor assesses
workflow.detail: The surveyor reviews the damage map and flags, then records the assessment in the motor claims system.

inputs: Guided photos or short video of the damaged vehicle
RC, driving licence and policy details
Claim intimation details: date, place and cause of loss
Parts catalogue and labour rates you use for assessment
outputs: Damage map by panel with damage type, severity and confidence
Photo quality and angle coverage report
human_in_the_loop: Licensed surveyors and loss assessors review every damage map and make the assessment, including what is payable. Both the model's suggestions and the surveyor's final decisions are logged, and corrections are used for retraining.
integrations: Self-inspection mobile app or WhatsApp Business API
Parts catalogue and labour rate master
Document extraction for RC and driving licence
guardrails: Suggestions only; no claim is settled or rejected by the model
Per-part confidence shown, with low-confidence parts marked for close review
Faces and third-party number plates blurred before images are used for training
Image metadata and duplicate checks run on every submission
Regular review of model performance by vehicle segment and lighting condition
compliance_notes: The assessment role of licensed surveyors and loss assessors under Indian insurance law is unchanged; the system prepares evidence for them.
Blurring bystanders and third-party plates before training supports data minimisation under the DPDP Act 2023.

pilot.scope: Historical, surveyor-closed own-damage claims for the most common private car segments, followed by a short live trial on new claims from a few network garages.
deliverables: Damage taxonomy and photo guide agreed with your surveyors
Detection models tuned on your historical claim photos
Roll-out plan, including two-wheeler and commercial vehicle extension

what_we_measure.how: Panels and damage types detected, compared with surveyor-finalised reports on the same claims.
Model suggestions compared with the surveyor's decision for each part.
Share of photo sets that needed one or more retakes during the live trial.
Surveyor feedback on each flagged estimate line.

faqs.a: No. It handles the repetitive first look and organises evidence, so surveyors spend their time on judgement. Where a surveyor is required, the surveyor still makes the assessment.

faqs.q: Does it work for two-wheelers and commercial vehicles?
faqs.a: The approach does, but each segment needs its own training data and photo guide. A typical plan starts with private cars and adds two-wheelers once enough surveyor-labelled claims are available.

faqs.q: How does it handle night photos, rain and dirt?
faqs.a: The quality check rejects images that are too dark or obscured and asks for a retake. Performance is reported separately for difficult conditions so you know where to rely on it.
It can price the suggested repairs using your own parts catalogue and labour rates. It does not invent prices, and the surveyor confirms the final figure.
